conventions.convention: The algebraic lemmas use even smooth chiral superfields, whose coefficient ring is commutative; dual vectors transform by right multiplication by the inverse.
Physical action brackets are [U]_D = −I_D(U)/4 and [Y]_F = I_F(Y)/2. Physical components satisfy ψ_raw = √2ψ and F_raw = 2F; Hermitian conjugation is added once to the extracted F coefficient.
The global group is SU(2), with T_a = −iσ_a/2, κ(X,Y) = −2Tr₂(XY), κ(T_a,T_b) = δ_ab, positive dimensionless g, mostly-plus Minkowski metric, and natural units c = ℏ = 1.
The N=2 adjoint vector chiral field is connection-normalized, Φ_can = Φ/g; its hypermultiplet fields Q and Q̃ are canonically normalized. The dual adjoint is identified using j(X)(Y) = κ_C(X,Y).
For N=4, φ_r = (X^(2r−1) + iX^(2r))/√2 and X_can^I = X^I/g. The potential sums over unordered pairs I < J with coefficient 1/(2g²) in connection normalization.

Eight- and sixteen-supercharge invariance are adopted classical model premises. Neither postulate constructs a quantum measure or continuum theory, proves extended invariance, or reports empirical evidence.

load_bearing.statement: Adopts a classical rigid four-dimensional N=2 SU(2) model with one hypermultiplet in a chosen finite-dimensional unitary representation, connection-normalized vector chiral field, quadratic ultraviolet prepotential iκ_C(Φ,Φ)/(2g²), and hypermultiplet superpotential √2 Q̃ρ_R*(Φ)Q + mQ̃Q. Extended invariance is an adopted premise; no quantum continuum or empirical claim is included.

Adopts the classical rigid N=4 SU(2) action with one vector and three connection-normalized adjoint chiral multiplets, cubic superpotential √2κ_C(Φ₁,[Φ₂,Φ₃])/g², and scalar potential (1/(2g²))Σ_(I<J)κ([X^I,X^J],[X^I,X^J]). Its sixteen-supercharge invariance and on-shell closure are adopted, not proved.

For an invertible even chiral matrix U acting by Q′ = UQ, Q̃′ = Q̃U⁻¹, and M′ = UMU⁻¹, the chiral polynomials Q̃Q and Q̃MQ are invariant. Consequently √2Q̃MQ + mQ̃Q is invariant for every constant m ∈ C.
For traceless 2×2 matrices Φ₁, Φ₂, Φ₃ over the even chiral coefficient ring, simultaneous conjugation by any invertible even chiral U preserves κ_C(Φ₁,[Φ₂,Φ₃]) and every constant multiple.
